# p0_gcp_cloud_logging (Resource)

A Google Cloud Logging log source installation for one project: P0 reads the project's Cloud Audit Logs, so that Access Logs can show what each request's access was used for.

**Important:** Before creating this resource you must stage the log source with `p0_gcp_cloud_logging_staged`, and deploy the following in the host project, with the names that staging returns:

- The connector's service account, `connector_service_account`, granted `roles/logging.privateLogViewer` on the project, so that it can read Data Access logs.
- The connector's Cloud Run service, `connector_service_name` in `region`, from P0's pinned connector image, running as that service account. It needs no VPC access.
- `roles/run.invoker` and `roles/run.viewer` on the service for P0's service account, the `service_account_email` of `p0_gcp`.

Creating this resource has P0 find the service's URL and check, through the connector, that it can read the project's Cloud Audit Logs. P0 retries for about 15 seconds while new IAM bindings take effect, then the apply fails with P0's message. If the first apply is denied access, apply again.

A log source that P0 hasn't finished installing, such as one imported before its install check passed, plans an update, and applying it finishes the install.

**Prerequisite:** P0's Google Cloud integration must be installed for your organization (see `p0_gcp`). P0 invokes the connector as that installation's service account.

**Note:** Access Logs is in beta. P0 offers this resource only to organizations that have Access Logs turned on.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Installs a Google Cloud Logging log source for one project: P0's connector on
# Cloud Run, which reads the project's Cloud Audit Logs so that Access Logs can
# show what each request's access was used for. For every project in your
# organization at once, see p0_gcp_organization_cloud_logging.
#
# Full chain: p0_gcp (see its example) -> p0_gcp_cloud_logging_staged -> the
# connector's service account, its roles/logging.privateLogViewer binding and
# its Cloud Run service -> roles/run.invoker and roles/run.viewer for P0's
# service account -> p0_gcp_cloud_logging.
#
# The host project needs the Service Usage API enabled. Cloud Run pulls the
# connector image from Docker Hub; Terraform checks its digest there on every
# plan.

terraform {
  # Reading the staged resource's attributes while it is still planned needs
  # Terraform 1.2.
  required_version = ">= 1.2"

  required_providers {
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = ">= 6.0"
    }
    docker = {
      source  = "kreuzwerker/docker"
      version = ">= 3.3, < 5.0"
    }
    # 0.98.0 added the log-source resources.
    p0 = {
      source  = "p0-security/p0"
      version = ">= 0.98.0"
    }
  }
}

locals {
  # The project whose Cloud Audit Logs P0 reads.
  project_id = "my-project-123"
  # The project the connector runs in. It can run the connectors of several
  # projects.
  host_project_id = "my-connector-project"

  # P0's connector image: its tag on Docker Hub, and the digest that tag must
  # resolve to. To update, take both from the latest version of this example in
  # the Terraform registry: they change together.
  connector_image_name   = "p0security/p0-connector-session-logging-gcp"
  connector_image_tag    = "sha-a266a1e"
  connector_image_digest = "sha256:cd33a3c9149e9318d461e9040756256ebe54aa2cf0a4c8b59a3016d218466f7c"
}

# Staging records the log source in P0, which answers with the connector's
# service name, service account and region.
resource "p0_gcp_cloud_logging_staged" "example" {
  project_id      = local.project_id
  host_project_id = local.host_project_id

  depends_on = [p0_gcp.example]
}

locals {
  log_source = p0_gcp_cloud_logging_staged.example
}

# Reads the image's digest from Docker Hub. It never talks to a Docker daemon.
provider "docker" {
  disable_docker_daemon_check = true
}

# Stops the plan if the tag has been moved to another image since P0 pinned it,
# so that only the image P0 pinned is deployed.
data "docker_registry_image" "connector" {
  name = "${local.connector_image_name}:${local.connector_image_tag}"

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = self.sha256_digest == local.connector_image_digest
      error_message = "The connector image's tag doesn't resolve to the digest pinned here. Take both from the latest p0_gcp_cloud_logging example in P0's Terraform registry docs, or contact support@p0.dev."
    }
  }
}

# The IAM and Cloud Run APIs. Never disabled on destroy: other services in the
# project may use them.
resource "google_project_service" "connector" {
  for_each = toset(["iam.googleapis.com", "run.googleapis.com"])

  project            = local.host_project_id
  service            = each.key
  disable_on_destroy = false
}

# The identity the connector runs as: the service account P0 generated when it
# staged the log source.
resource "google_service_account" "connector" {
  project      = local.host_project_id
  account_id   = split("@", local.log_source.connector_service_account)[0]
  display_name = "P0 Google Cloud Logging connector"

  depends_on = [google_project_service.connector]
}

# The connector reads this project's Cloud Audit Logs, Data Access logs
# included.
resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_log_viewer" {
  project = local.project_id
  role    = "roles/logging.privateLogViewer"
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# No VPC access: the connector calls only Google's public APIs.
resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service" "connector" {
  project             = local.host_project_id
  name                = local.log_source.connector_service_name
  location            = local.log_source.region
  deletion_protection = false
  # P0 calls the connector from outside Google Cloud. IAM, not the caller's
  # network, controls access.
  ingress = "INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL"

  template {
    service_account = google_service_account.connector.email

    containers {
      image = "docker.io/${local.connector_image_name}:${local.connector_image_tag}@${data.docker_registry_image.connector.sha256_digest}"

      # The connector checks every caller's token against this, and refuses
      # every call while it's unset.
      env {
        name  = "INVOKER_SA_EMAIL"
        value = p0_gcp.example.service_account_email
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.connector]
}

# P0 invokes the connector as its own service account.
resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "p0_invoker" {
  project  = local.host_project_id
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.invoker"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

# P0 reads the service to find its URL when it installs. The invoker role can't
# do this read.
resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "p0_viewer" {
  project  = local.host_project_id
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.viewer"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

# Completes the install. P0 finds the connector's URL and checks that it can read
# the project's Cloud Audit Logs. A new IAM binding can take a minute to take
# effect, so if the first apply is denied access, apply again.
resource "p0_gcp_cloud_logging" "example" {
  project_id      = local.log_source.project_id
  host_project_id = local.log_source.host_project_id

  depends_on = [
    google_project_iam_member.connector_log_viewer,
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.p0_invoker,
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.p0_viewer,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host_project_id` (String) The Google Cloud project that the connector runs in, on Cloud Run
- `project_id` (String) The Google Cloud project whose Cloud Audit Logs P0 reads

### Read-Only

- `connector_service_account` (String) The email of the service account that the connector runs as, in the host project, which P0 generates when it stages the log source
- `connector_service_name` (String) The name of the connector's Cloud Run service, which P0 generates when it stages the log source
- `connector_service_uri` (String) The connector's Cloud Run URL, which P0 reads from the deployed service when it installs the log source
- `region` (String) The region that the connector's Cloud Run service runs in, which P0 chooses when it stages the log source
- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed
